Assessment.source_text: Um, it seems like you may have something, uh, called gastroenteritis, which essentially just a tummy bug or infection of your uh of your tummy.

Assessment.content: Gastroenteritis is mainly viral though bacterial causes are possible.
Assessment.source_text: Uh, mainly caused by viruses but there can be a possibility of bacteria uh causing its symptoms.

Plan_of_Care.content: Conservative management recommended; antibiotics are not needed at this stage.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: At this stage, uh, what, what we'd recommend is just what we say conservative management. So, um, I don't think you need anything like antibiotics.

Plan_of_Care.content: Ensure adequate hydration by drinking fluids.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: It's really just, um, making sure you're well hydrated, so drinking fluids.

Plan_of_Care.content: Use oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte from the pharmacy.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: there are things like Dioralyte you can get from the pharmacy, which uh it's um it helps helps replenish your minerals and vitamins.

Plan_of_Care.content: Take paracetamol, two tablets up to four times daily for the first few days if feverish or weak.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: If you are feeling feverish and weak, eh taking some paracetamol, uh, two tablets up to four times a day for the first few days can also help.

Plan_of_Care.content: Take two to three days off work to rest while the infection clears.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I will certainly advise you to take some time off work, actually I know you're quite keen to work but I would say the next two, two to three days as the infection clears from your system to take some time off and rest.

Follow_up_Information.content: Return for review in three to four days if symptoms have not improved.
